notes: Every case starts from a clean state: click #resetBtn, then apply the 'baseline' block at the top of this file in the order given, then apply the case's (or the state's) own 'controls' block on top of it. The page's shipped defaults are NOT the baseline: out of the box #adults is 2, #hasCard is ticked with a $10,000 limit and #newPropCosts is $350/mo, so every one of those is restated in the baseline.

Setting controls. Text inputs with class fmt-num or fmt-pct (#incSimple, #incPayg, #declaredExp, #price, #savings, #prodRate, #termYears, #umiReq, ...) take a plain number string with no separators: set .value, dispatch 'input' and 'change', then blur. Range inputs (#incSplit, #deps, #buffer, #floorRate, #nsrMin, #cardPct, #lvrMax, #dtiCap): set .value then dispatch 'input' and 'change'; a range silently clamps to its own min/max, which two cases rely on. Selects (#city, #adults, #taxYear, #helpMode, #olType, #occupancy, #depositMode, #dutyMode, #dtiBasis): set .value and dispatch 'change'. Checkboxes and toggle switches (#hasCard, #privHealth, #lmiCap, #hasIo, #negGear, ...): click only when the current .checked differs from the requested boolean.

Segmented controls (#incWhoGroup, #incModeGroup, #debtsModeGroup, #loanModeGroup, #capsModeGroup) are groups of buttons: click the button inside that group whose data-val equals the requested string, and confirm it ends up with class 'active'.
Quick Start presets are the buttons .quick-start-btn[data-preset='...'] above the tabs; a state that names 'preset' clicks that button and then applies any controls listed after it.

Some inputs only exist once their tick box or tab mode is on. Apply controls in the order written: the tick boxes (#hasCard, #hasInvest, ...) and the Simple/Detailed segmented controls always come before the fields they reveal.

A state may carry, in this order: 'preset' (click that Quick Start button first), 'controls' (apply these), 'then_preset' (click a second Quick Start button without resetting) and 'then' (apply these last). 'then' exists so a case can fill a field and then untick the box that revealed it, which is the whole point of B10.

Observables come from the six KPI cards (#kpiLoan, #kpiBind, #kpiPrice, #kpiRepay, #kpiNsr, #kpiUmi and their .sub lines), the four tables (#capsTableWrap 'The four caps', #buildTableWrap 'Serviceability build-up', #incomeTableWrap 'Income shading', #commTableWrap 'Monthly commitments'), #warnBanner, and the small notes #hemNote, #depositNote, #lvrSimpleNote. Report every money figure as a plain number (strip $ and thousands separators, keep the sign), every percentage as a plain number in percent, and text verbatim. Report a quantity that is genuinely not on the page as null rather than guessing.

Several observables are derived: they are arithmetic the runner does on figures it has already read, and the key's 'what' states the arithmetic. Never compute finance maths of your own to fill one - only add, subtract or divide numbers the page printed.

Cases with 'states' are several independent states of the page. Apply each from a clean state (Reset -> baseline -> that state's controls) and prefix the observation keys as the observe list names them.

cases.title: Baseline: single PAYG applicant, no debts, 20% deposit - the build-up adds up line by line

observe.what: The assessment rate the page says it tested you at, in percent (look in #kpiRepaySub, the Serviceability build-up, or the caps table).
Assessed monthly repayment, the value of #kpiRepay.
UMI, the value of #kpiUmi, as a monthly dollar figure.
Max purchase price, the value of #kpiPrice.
Total gross annual income before shading, from the total row of the Income shading table.
Total assessed (shaded) annual income, from the total row of the Income shading table.

Total annual tax the Serviceability build-up charges the household: income tax plus Medicare levy plus any surcharge plus any study-loan repayment treated as tax. If the build-up shows one combined tax line, report it; if it shows several tax lines, report their sum; if it shows monthly figures, multiply by 12. Report as a positive number.
The monthly after-tax income the Serviceability build-up carries into the surplus calculation. If the build-up is annual, divide by 12.
The monthly living-cost figure the build-up actually uses (the higher of declared expenses and HEM).
Total monthly existing commitments, from the total row of the Monthly commitments table (0 if the table is empty).
Derived: net_income_monthly - living_monthly - commitments_monthly - assessed_repayment - umi.
The serviceability cap's dollar value in the 'The four caps' table.
The debt-to-income cap's dollar value in the 'The four caps' table.
The loan-to-value cap's dollar value in the 'The four caps' table.
The deposit cap's dollar value in the 'The four caps' table.
Count of occurrences of 'NaN', 'Infinity', '-0', 'undefined' or 'null' in the visible text of the six KPI cards and the four tables (0 when none).
